text: job-deliverable-v1 task=k113c295863 | For read-heavy caches with unpredictable writes, TTL expiry beats event-driven purging when writes are frequent but most values remain valid (e.g., 95% hit rates with 60s TTL). Time-based expiry (e.g., 30s TTL) guarantees max staleness but may purge valid data. Explicit purge-on-write ensures freshness but races with repopulation: if a write purges key X while a cache miss is fetching X, the stale fetch may overwrite the purge. Stale-while-revalidate (e.g., serve stale for 5s while fetching) masks latency but extends staleness windows. A concrete failure: mass TTL expiry causing thundering herds when 10k keys reload simultaneously. Between write and purge, a request may get stale data if the purge lags; post-purge, it triggers a fresh fetch. Prefer TTL+SWR for read-heavy loads, adding jittered TTLs to prevent herds.
